ap_physics_1-f01.title: Crate pulled by a rope at an angle across a rough floor

stimulus.description: A crate of mass $m=10\text{ kg}$ is pulled across a rough horizontal floor by a rope that exerts a force of magnitude $T=60\text{ N}$ at an angle $\theta=20^\circ$ above the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the crate and the floor is $\mu=0.25$. The crate speeds up as it slides.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: On the dot below, which represents the crate, draw and label the forces (not components) that act on the crate while it slides. Each force must be represented by a distinct arrow starting on the dot.
parts.model_answer: Four arrows from the dot: weight straight down, the normal force straight up, the rope force up and to the right at the angle $\theta$, and kinetic friction to the left. The normal force is shorter than the weight because the rope pulls partly upward.

rubric_rows.criterion: Draws and labels all four forces: weight (down), normal force (up), rope tension (up and to the right) and kinetic friction (left), with no extra force
common_errors: adds a force of motion
omits the normal force

rubric_rows.criterion: Directions are correct: the rope force at the angle above the horizontal toward the direction of motion and friction opposite to the motion
common_errors: draws friction in the direction of motion

rubric_rows.criterion: The normal force arrow is shorter than the weight arrow because the rope has an upward component
common_errors: draws the normal force equal to the weight

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the magnitude of the acceleration of the crate in terms of $m$, $T$, $\theta$, $\mu$, and fundamental constants.

rubric_rows.criterion: Applies the vertical equilibrium condition to find the normal force: $N=mg-T\sin\theta$
required_elements: N = m g - T sin theta
common_errors: uses N = m g

rubric_rows.criterion: Writes Newton's second law along the floor: $T\cos\theta-\mu N=ma$
required_elements: T cos theta - mu N = m a
common_errors: uses the full tension in the horizontal equation

rubric_rows.criterion: Combines the equations to the correct expression for $a$
required_elements: (T cos theta - mu (m g - T sin theta))/m
common_errors: omits the upward component of the rope force from the normal force

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of the crate for $m=10\text{ kg}$, $T=60\text{ N}$, $\theta=20^\circ$ and $\mu=0.25$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the normal force (about 77 newtons) from the expression in part B
common_errors: uses mg as the normal force

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates an acceleration of about 3.70 with units of meters per second squared
common_errors: uses the weight as the normal force

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: The rope is raised so that the angle increases by $10^\circ$, while the tension stays the same and the crate keeps sliding. Does the magnitude of the kinetic friction force increase, decrease, or stay the same? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The friction force decreases. A larger angle gives the rope a larger upward component $T\sin\theta$, which lowers the normal force $N=mg-T\sin\theta$, and $f=\mu N$ decreases.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the kinetic friction force decreases
common_errors: states that friction stays the same because the crate weighs the same

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies that the larger upward component of the rope force reduces the normal force, and friction is proportional to the normal force
common_errors: argues only that the horizontal component of the tension decreases
